sn45.159:1.1: “Bhikkhus, suppose there is a guest house. People come from the east, west, north, and south and lodge there; khattiyas, brahmins, vessas, and suddas come and lodge there.
sn45.159:1.2: So too, when a bhikkhu develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path, he fully understands by direct knowledge those things that are to be fully understood by direct knowledge;
sn45.159:1.3: he abandons by direct knowledge those things that are to be abandoned by direct knowledge; he realizes by direct knowledge those things that are to be realized by direct knowledge; he develops by direct knowledge those things that are to be developed by direct knowledge.
sn45.159:2.1: “And what, bhikkhus, are the things to be fully understood by direct knowledge?
sn45.159:2.2: It should be said: the five aggregates subject to clinging.
sn45.159:2.4: The form aggregate subject to clinging … the consciousness aggregate subject to clinging.
sn45.159:2.5: These are the things to be fully understood by direct knowledge.
sn45.159:2.6: “And what, bhikkhus, are the things to be abandoned by direct knowledge?
sn45.159:2.8: These are the things to be abandoned by direct knowledge.
sn45.159:2.9: “And what, bhikkhus, are the things to be realized by direct knowledge?
sn45.159:2.11: These are the things to be realized by direct knowledge.
sn45.159:2.12: “And what, bhikkhus, are the things to be developed by direct knowledge?
sn45.159:2.14: These are the things to be developed by direct knowledge.
sn45.159:2.15: “And how is it, bhikkhus, that when a bhikkhu develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path, he fully understands by direct knowledge those things that are to be fully understood by direct knowledge … … he develops by direct knowledge those things that are to be developed by direct knowledge?
sn45.159:2.16: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view … right concentration, which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, maturing in release.
sn45.159:2.17: It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path so that he fully understands by direct knowledge those things that are to be fully understood by direct knowledge … he develops by direct knowledge those things that are to be developed by direct knowledge.”
